research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google: narrative prompt (subject + action + location + composition + style), put exact in-image text in quotes and name its typography, name lens/camera/film stock, design the light, specify materials (tweed not 'jacket'), phrase positively; 9:16 is supported
https://dev.to/googleai/getting-the-most-out-of-nano-banana-2-502k — Google's developer post: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) is strong at text rendering and complex styles
https://fliki.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-prompting-guide — practitioner: keep in-image text short and quoted; few text elements per image renders cleanest
https://runware.ai/docs/models/google-nano-banana-2/guides/prompting — describe the whole image (subject, style, light, composition), natural sentences over tag lists
https://en.wikipedia.com/wiki/On_His_Majesty%27s_Service — O.H.M.S. is the printed legend on UK government correspondence; current wording is His Majesty's
https://gcs.civilservice.gov.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/HMG_Identity-Guidelines_2022.pdf — UK government identity centres on a coat of arms; we invent our own crest instead

https://www.gov.uk/guidance/standard-individual-export-licences-siels — arms exports go out on a Standard Individual Export Licence issued by the Export Control Joint Unit, for named goods to a named end-user; supports the 'EXPORT LICENCE' paperwork inside the envelope

https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/687910bc7ea2091686363947/UK_Strategic_Export_Controls_Annual_Report_2024.pdf — 15,464 SIEL applications processed in 2024: this paperwork is routine and continuous, whichever party governs

https://learn.planetbanknote.com/how-banknotes-are-printed/ — banknotes are printed in sheets in several passes (offset litho, intaglio for raised detail, letterpress for serial numbers); gives real press-hall detail for beat C

https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2020/october/extension-to-de-la-rue-contract — UK notes are printed at a single secure facility in Essex; we depict an unnamed press hall with invented notes, no real design or company
notes: The three looks are matched across all beats: a = photographic 1970s Whitehall spy-film insert, b = two-colour linocut / screenprint, c = handmade stop-motion miniature. So A and B rhyme (same desk, same envelope, same overhead angle, only the stamp changes), and C carries each look through to the print room. Pick a column (a, b or c) and it cuts as one short. Stamps are the only long text; each prompt names the exact words in quotes and keeps other text to 'O.H.M.S.' and 'EXPORT LICENCE'. The crest is invented (a crowned key between two herons). No faces, no logos, no real banknote designs; hands only, in shirt cuffs. Check the stamp spelling on every take before picking: long rubber-stamp text is the likeliest thing to come back misspelled. No BadCode figure appears, so the balaclava sentence is not used.

stills.prompt: A vertical 9:16 overhead insert shot, like a 1970s British espionage film: a stiff buff government envelope has just dropped onto a scuffed green leather desk top in a Whitehall office, still sliding, a corner lifting. Printed at the top: "O.H.M.S." beside a small invented crest of a crowned key between two herons, and "EXPORT LICENCE" in typewriter capitals. Across the middle, a slightly crooked red rubber stamp in heavy block capitals reads exactly "APPROVED BY THE CONSERVATIVE PARTY", the ink pooling at one edge. A brass banker's lamp throws warm tungsten light from the left; a cold grey window spills blue from the right. Kodak 35mm film stock, 40mm lens, fine grain, a ring stain from a teacup. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 linocut print in two inks only, black and a hot vermilion red, on off-white rough rag paper with visible gouge marks and slightly uneven ink. Seen from directly above: a large envelope falling flat onto a desk, carved speed lines behind it, a single bare hand in a shirt cuff just letting go at the top edge. The envelope carries a small carved crest of a crowned key between two herons and the words "O.H.M.S.". Stamped across it in red, in chunky carved block letters, exactly "APPROVED BY THE CONSERVATIVE PARTY". The desk grain is cut as bold parallel lines; a fountain pen and a blotter sit beside it. Misregistration of the red by a few millimetres, like a hand-pulled print. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 macro photograph of a handmade stop-motion miniature set: a tiny civil-service desk built from real balsa and dark-stained card, a felt blotter, a thumbnail-sized brass lamp with a warm LED glow. A small paper envelope, hand-cut and slightly wonky, hangs mid-drop on a visible thread just above the desk. It reads "O.H.M.S." with a hand-painted crest of a crowned key between two herons, and a red stamp painted in careful block letters reading exactly "APPROVED BY THE CONSERVATIVE PARTY". Fingerprints in the plasticine paperweight, dust on the set, shallow depth of field from a 100mm macro lens, a painted Whitehall window backdrop out of focus behind. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph in the style of a 1970s British industrial documentary: a long, low banknote press hall under buzzing fluorescent tubes, a huge green-painted sheet-fed printing press running at speed, motion blur on its rollers. Uncut sheets of invented banknotes, in a muted purple and olive with an engraved heron and a crowned key, spill out of the delivery end and stack into a tall leaning pile. Nobody stands at the controls; an empty swivel chair, a clipboard and two buff envelopes stamped in red lie forgotten on a steel bench in the foreground. Kodak 35mm stock, 28mm lens, fine grain, oil sheen on the concrete floor. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 linocut print in two inks only, black and hot vermilion red, on rough off-white rag paper with visible gouge marks. A monstrous carved printing press fills the frame, gears and rollers cut as bold black shapes, carved motion lines showing it running flat out. From its mouth pours an endless ribbon of invented banknotes, each simply cut with a heron and a crowned key and printed in red, curling up and out of the top of the frame. At its foot, small and flattened, two envelopes lie on the floor beside a tipped-over ballot box. The red slightly out of register, like a hand-pulled proof. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 macro photograph of a handmade stop-motion miniature: a tabletop printing press built from brass clock gears, a cotton reel for a roller and painted card, turned by a small crank. Tiny invented banknotes, hand-printed in faded purple and olive with a heron and a crowned key, fly out of it on visible threads and pile up in a heap taller than the press. Beside the heap, on a tiny balsa desk, two paper envelopes with red stamps sit ignored under a thumbnail-sized brass lamp. Warm practical light, dust, glue strings, fingerprints in the plasticine floor, shallow depth of field from a 100mm macro lens. Thanks.
